newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK Stagecoach bonanza ends stormy year.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK Stagecoach bonanza ends stormy year.

text.p: Britain's Stagecoach Plc delivered a near-trebling of profits on Tuesday in a results bonanza which marked the end of a stormy year of scathing criticism from rail watchdogs and passengers alike over widescale train cancellations last spring.

Pretax profits for the year ended April 30 were 120.5 million pounds ($201.6 million) compared with 43.6 million a year earlier. Sales, helped by acquisitions, leapt to 1.152 billion pounds from 501.2 million and the annual dividend was raised to nine pence from 6.7 pence.

Brian Souter, executive chairman, described the results as "excellent", just months after the bus and railway company was dogged by criticism over disruptions at its South West Trains (SWT) rail franchise when it axed 10 percent of its drivers.
Stagecoach shares initially jumped on the news but later staged a sharp about turn, falling six pence to 731 after touching a high of 765.

The group came close to a one million pounds fine from rail watchdog Opraf over SWT and paid out 1.5 million in voluntary compensation to irate passengers who suffered hundreds of train cancellations.
But Stagecoach profits emerged unscathed, with the surge fuelled by its recent expansion spending spree.
"These are quality results from an increasingly quality company," said Nigel Hawkins, analyst at Yamaichi.
Richard Hannah, analyst at UBS, said the results had topped his forecast of 112 million, citing rolling stock company Porterbrook as the catalyst for the dynamic profit growth.

Souter said of the performance:"These achievements reflect further developments in our core bus businesses in the UK and overseas; a first full- year contribution from SWT; the impact of the current year acquisitions of Porterbrook and Swebus (the Swedish bus company)."
Profits were further bolstered by 15.2 million pounds in proceeds from the sale of a stake in Strathclyde Buses.
Stagecoach said the current year had "started well" and that prospects looked good. Souter said he believed the group's expansion programme would deliver "strong growth in earnings for the future".

Souter said its SWT unit was now back on track after its problems. He said the group's aim was "to deliver consistent quality over the remaining six years of the franchise" in the hope of getting an extension to its term to run the rail service.

Looking to the year ahead, finance director Keith Cochrane said on the domestic bus front, growth would be organic. He ruled out major acquisitions in Britain, telling Reuters, "UK bus acquisition prices at the moment are too high due to regulatory uncertainty."
The finance chief said Stagecoach would concentrate its ambitions on sealing a follow-up deal to Swebus in another continental European country.

The group's African bus businesses remained a worry, with Kenya hit by renewed political turmoil over demands for democratic elections and the Malawi business seeing margins suffer from "unregulated competition".
Cochrane told Reuters the Malawi operation was up for review and one option was to "downsize the business to a profitable core and focus on intercity routes."
Looking at a divisional breakdown of the results, continued British bus operations saw turnover up to 450.5 million, versus 388.3 million, with profits to 67.4 million from 58.3 million.
African bus operations saw turnover up to 37.3 million versus 34.0 million, with profits down to 3.3 million versus 4.5 million.
New Zealand turnover was 15.4 million, up from 14.8 million, but profits fell to 2.7 million from 3.5 million.
South West Trains saw turnover up to 283.4 million versus 63.4 million -- reflecting the first full year of its inclusion. Profits were 8.0 million versus 400,000 pounds.
The newly acquired businesses, comprising mainly of Porterbrook and Swebus, provided turnover of 353.9 million and profits of 86.9 million.

Since the end of the results period, Stagecoach concluded its acquisitions of Thames Transit Ltd and Docklands Transit Ltd for 8.2 million in cash , with a further one million linked to performance targets.
It has also finalised a 3.7 million pound acquisition of part of Transit Australia, a 120-strong bus operation in Queensland. ($ = 0.597 British Pounds)
